name: Titus
overview: Titus is a male believer recognized as a brother and a close partner of the Apostle Paul in ministry. He is noted for his faithful service and cooperation with Paul, particularly in the context of the early Christian church. Scripture highlights his role as a fellow worker, emphasizing his trusted position alongside Paul.
namesAndTitles: The name Titus appears in Scripture without an accompanying meaning or divine naming significance. It is simply presented as his proper name.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Titus beyond his identification as a brother and ministry partner of Paul. There are no additional familial ties mentioned.
scriptureSignificance: Titus holds a significant place in the New Testament as a trusted companion and co-laborer with Paul. His role as a brother and fellow worker underscores the importance of partnership in advancing the gospel. Titus’s ministry partnership with Paul reflects the collaborative nature of early church leadership and the spread of the Christian faith.
